claims.statement: OCPI defines the CDR as the billing-relevant object for a completed charging session; sent CDRs cannot be changed or deleted and corrections use a linked credit CDR.
The OCPI project explicitly supports session and CDR exchange and lists invoice reconciliation in its specification contents.
EU implementing rules adopted in 2025 require more compatible, interoperable, and real-time alternative-fuels infrastructure data.

contrary_evidence: OCPI already contains invoice-reconciliation concepts, so the opportunity depends on operational adoption and shared governance rather than a missing data format.
Existing roaming hubs and charge-point-management vendors are natural incumbents for this function.

economics.acquisition_route: A paid reconciliation audit followed by a narrow bilateral live lane, then member referrals and OCPI integration partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year path would require roughly 20-30 million annual CDRs at about 0.05 EUR average usage revenue plus member subscriptions, disciplined support costs, and founder ownership of a network-valued software business
economics.founder_time: Approximately 15-18 hours per week during early bilateral integrations, declining as connectors standardise
economics.gross_margin_basis: Protocol ingestion, rules execution, and exception support less high-availability infrastructure and partner onboarding
economics.payback: A member can justify the service through fewer finance hours, faster credits, and reduced leakage; real mismatch rates and disputed value require transaction samples
economics.pricing: Approximately 500-2,000 EUR monthly per member plus 0.03-0.10 EUR per reconciled CDR depending on volume
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every charging session and monthly invoice produces recurring records; bilateral acceptance creates operational switching cost

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Each bilateral connection makes the shared exception taxonomy and counterparty reliability history more useful, supporting lower-cost onboarding and earlier error detection
fingerprint.customer: Smaller and regional EU charge-point operators, e-mobility service providers, fleet charging platforms, and roaming intermediaries
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Start with one fleet platform and its regional CPO counterparties, then recruit through OCPI implementers and charging-industry associations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: OCPI connectors, immutable reconciliation ledger, bilateral exception workflow, credit-CDR handling, and bank-ready net payable files
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Members pay a base subscription and a few euro cents when a CDR is matched, cleared, or converted into a documented dispute packet
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Month-end invoices do not match session, tariff, CDR, credit, or tax records across bilateral roaming relationships

founder_fit: The reconciliation engine is a strong match for quantitative and data-engineering skills
A protocol-first product can be built without consumer brand exposure
The initial service can avoid custody by sending approved net files to existing payment providers
risks: The two-sided member cold start may stall
Tax invoice and metering rules vary by jurisdiction
A bad netting instruction could create material liability
Established roaming hubs may add equivalent reconciliation

structure.commercial_archetype: Member clearing network charging subscription and per-record fees
structure.control_point: The canonical bilateral charge-detail-record lineage, including tariff snapshot, immutable original, credit record, dispute state, and accepted invoice mapping
structure.critical_dependency: Enough counterparties must contribute complete OCPI data and contractually accept common reconciliation and dispute rules

thesis: Regional EV charge-point operators, mobility providers, and fleet networks could join a neutral proof-clearing service that matches OCPI sessions, tariffs, charge detail records, credits, and invoices; applies a bilateral dispute clock; and produces a net-payable file for existing payment providers. The scarce asset would be accepted cross-party CDR lineage, not another consumer charging app.
title: RoamNet Proof Clearing
uncertainties: Observed CDR mismatch rates among regional operators
Whether parties will accept a neutral dispute clock and data retention terms
Availability of signed metering data at sufficient quality
The smallest bilateral volume at which integration produces clear payback
